get.summary:
Lists audit entries, newest first (by time, then by id). With no dates the range is today and the 6 business days before it; a date
is a business day (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Manila time) from the start of the kept window (8 months) to today, and the range includes the
whole of both days. An actor also matches a person's own sign-in, code, reset and invitation steps. The detail holds the stored
fixed words only: field names and role values, never a name or an email address (D-40).

Lists everyone the Done by and Done to filters can offer: every person ever recorded as staff, active or inactive by name first,
then former staff by name. Names only, never an email address.

post.summary: Sets the first password from an invite. It issues no session.
Tells the accept-invite page whether its link still works and which account it is for.
Emails a reset link when the address belongs to an active staff account. Every well-formed address gets the same answer.
Sets a new password from a reset link. It ends every session and signs nobody in.
Tells the reset page whether its link still works and which account it is for.
Saves the new password of an account that must change it, and only then signs the person in (D-13, D-22).
Tells the must-change screen who the pending sign-in is for and why, on every arrival. It never spends the ticket.
Renews the access token with the refresh cookie and rotates the cookie.
Checks the email and password and sends the sign-in code.
Ends this device's session and clears the refresh cookie. It succeeds with no cookie too.
Ends every other session of the signed-in user and keeps this one. It succeeds when there is nothing to end.
Sends a new sign-in code for the pending ticket, after the cooldown and within the hourly cap.
Checks the emailed code and starts the session, or hands over to the set-new-password step.

get.summary:
Lists expenses, newest first by expense date, then by when they were recorded, then by id. With neither date the window runs
from 30 days before to 30 days after today in the business zone, and the answer says which dates and which today it used.
The total and the period total cover every page of the filter. Both roles see every expense; `canEdit` says whether the
caller may edit a row. Notes are never listed or searched.

post.summary:
Records an expense. The date may be any past day and up to 30 days after today in the business zone, the amount is above
0.00 and at most 1,000,000.00 with two decimal places, and the payer must be an active Admin or Manager who has signed in at least once.
A retired category is refused. Who recorded it and when come from the token and the clock; any such member in the
body is ignored. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored 201 and records nothing more.

parameters.description: Search text for the description or the payer's or recorder's name; blank means no search.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: A category id; none means all.
parameters.name: category

parameters.description: Rows per page, from 1 to 100; 20 when not sent.
parameters.name: pageSize

get.summary:
Lists the deleted expenses, Managers only, most recently deleted first and then by id. Each row says who deleted it and when.
The total covers every page of the filter. There is no period total, and notes are never listed or searched.

Reads the month figures for the expenses page: this month and last month, each with its total and count, and this month's top
category with its share. Months follow the business zone, expenses count by their date (upcoming ones included) and deleted
expenses never count. The list filters do not apply.

delete.summary:
Deletes one expense, Managers only. The expense stays in the database but leaves the list, its total, the month KPIs and the
detail, and an edit of it answers 404. Who deleted it and when are recorded, and Last changed by follows. It takes no version:
it acts on the latest state, and deleting an expense that is already deleted is a 404 that changes nothing.

get.summary: Reads one expense with its version, who recorded it and last changed it, and whether the caller may edit it.

put.summary:
Saves an edit of one expense with the version the form was opened with. The field rules are the same as when recording. A
version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form edit is never retried. A Manager
may edit any expense and an Admin only one they recorded or paid. A payer who is changed must be an active Admin or Manager
who has signed in at least once, and a category that is changed must not be retired; a saved payer or category may stay. Who changed it
and when come from the token and the clock; any such member in the body is ignored. A form with no change saves nothing.

delete.summary:
Deletes one expense for good, Managers only, whether or not it was deleted before. The row is removed from the database and there
is no way back. The audit log keeps one entry with the date, category, amount and payer, and never the description or notes. It
takes no version, and removing an expense that is already gone is a 404 that changes nothing.

post.summary:
Restores a deleted expense, Managers only: it counts again in the list, its total, the month KPIs and the detail. Last changed by
is the Manager who restored it. Restoring an expense that is not deleted is a 204 that changes and records nothing. It takes no
version, and a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the stored 204.

get.summary:
Lists every category, retired ones included with status `retired`, A to Z with Others always last, then by id. Each item
says how many expenses use the category, soft-deleted ones included. The Add picker hides retired ones; the list filter keeps them.

post.summary:
Adds a category, Managers only. The name is required, at most 40 characters and unique among all categories, retired ones
included, ignoring letter case. The tone is one of six: `neutral`, `accent`, `info`, `mockup`,
`warning` or `success`. Who added it and when come from the token and the clock; any such member in the body is
ignored. A retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body answers with the stored 201 and adds nothing more.

get.summary: Reads one category with how many expenses use it, who recorded and last changed it, and the version a save must send back. Managers only.

put.summary:
Renames and recolors one category with the version the form was opened with, Managers only. The new name shows on every
expense, past ones included. The name and tone follow the same rules as when adding. Others keeps its name but may change
colour. A version that is not the stored one answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing; a form edit is never retried.
A form with no change saves nothing and keeps the version. Who changed it and when come from the token and the clock; any such
member in the body is ignored.

post.summary:
Brings a retired category back, Managers only: it can be chosen on a new expense again. Bringing back an active category is a
204 that changes and records nothing. It takes no version, and a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the
stored 204.

Retires a category, Managers only: it can no longer be chosen on a new expense but stays in the list and the list filter,
marked `retired`, and old expenses keep it. Others can never be retired. Retiring a retired category is a 204 that
changes and records nothing. It takes no version, and a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers with the stored 204.

get.summary: Reads the caller's profile, including the edit version the next save must send.

put.summary: Changes the caller's first and last name. The version must be the one the form was opened with.

delete.summary:
Calls off the waiting email change: its links stop working and the pending address is cleared. Naturally idempotent, so it
takes no row version and answers 204 when nothing is waiting.

post.summary:
Asks to change the caller's sign-in email. A confirmation link goes to the new address and a notice to the current one; the
sign-in email changes only when the link is confirmed.

Tells the confirm-email page whether its link still works and which address it would confirm. Anonymous and read-only: it
spends nothing and changes nothing, so a mail scanner opening the link confirms nothing. The token travels in the body.

Confirms an email change from the emailed link. Anonymous: the link is the proof, so the person need not be signed in. The
token travels in the body, never in a URL.

Sends a fresh 24-hour confirmation link to the waiting new address and kills the older one (D-24). Nothing goes to the
current address, and no address is written.
Changes the caller's password after checking the current one. Every other device is signed out; this one stays signed in.

get.summary: Lists the caller's own active sessions: this device first, then the rest by recent activity, at most 100.

delete.summary: Signs out one of the caller's other devices. Repeating the call is a success.

200.description: The settings, or the failure as ProblemDetails.

get.summary:
Lists the people who can be named as the payer: an Admin or Manager who is active, not locked by a Manager, not deleted
and has signed in at least once (entered a sign-in code or accepted an invite). Someone a Manager just added with a
temporary password appears after their first sign-in code. Sorted by first name, last name, then id.

parameters.description: Search text for the name or email; blank means no search.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Rows per page, from 1 to 100; 20 when not sent.
parameters.name: pageSize

get.summary: Lists staff, sorted by first name, then last name, then id. A page past the last returns no rows and the true total.

post.summary:
Adds a staff member (USER-02). By invitation the account has no password and a 7-day link is emailed; with a temporary
password the Manager hands it over and the person must replace it at first sign-in. The answer holds the new id only.

delete.summary:
Deletes a person for good (USER-03, D-07..D-11): they cannot sign in, every session and link of theirs ends at once, they leave the
roster and their detail answers 404, and their address is free for a new invitation. Records they created keep their name. There
is no way back. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state, and deleting someone already deleted is a 404 that changes
nothing. A Manager cannot delete their own account (422 `users.own-account`) or the last active Manager (422
`users.last-active-manager`).

get.summary: Reads one person with their edit version and who created and last changed them (SEC-08).

put.summary:
Edits another person's name, sign-in email and role (USER-03). The version must be the one the form was opened with: any other
answers 409 `edit.stale` and changes nothing (SEC-07). A Manager cannot edit their own account here (422
`users.own-account`), and cannot demote the last active Manager (422 `users.last-active-manager`). A role change ends
every session of the person at once. Saving the values already stored is a 200 that changes and records nothing.
When the email differs from the stored one, `emailChange` must say how it applies (D-45), and a missing or unknown value is
a 400 on that field: `confirm` keeps the sign-in email and sends the new address a confirmation link that names the Manager,
with a notice to the old address (C-9), and the answer shows the new address as `pendingEmail`; `now` changes the email
in the same save, signs the person out everywhere and notifies the old address. A person invited but not yet set up always moves
at once and gets a fresh invitation at the new address. A taken address is a 400 on `email`. `emailChange` is ignored
when the email is unchanged.

post.summary: Reactivates a person (USER-03). Repeating it on an active person is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version.

Deactivates a person (USER-03): they cannot sign in and every session of theirs ends at once, so their next request with an old
token is a 401. Repeating it on an inactive person is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state.

delete.summary:
Calls off a person's waiting email change (USER-03, C-9): the open links stop working and the pending address is cleared. With
nothing waiting it is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state (D-21). A Manager uses My
Profile for their own account (422 `users.own-account`).

post.summary:
Locks a person (USER-03, D-16): they cannot sign in, a password reset does not help, and every session of theirs ends at once, so
their next request with an old token is a 401. The lock has no timer; only a Manager lifts it. It is separate from the 15-minute
failed-password lockout. Repeating it on a locked person is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version: it acts on the latest
state.

Sends a person who has not set a password a fresh 7-day invitation (USER-07, D-13). The earlier link stops working and the new one
goes to the person by email only; the answer never holds it. A person who already has a password is a 422
`users.already-set-up`, and a deactivated or locked one is a 422 `users.blocked`. It takes no version: it acts on the
latest state and does not change the account.

Emails a person a password reset link that they open themself (USER-07). The link names the Manager, works once for 30 minutes and
replaces any open reset link; the answer never holds it. It counts toward the same hourly cap of reset emails as forgot-password
(429 `users.reset-link-capped`). A deactivated or locked person is a 422 `users.blocked` and a person who never set a
password is a 422 `users.no-password`. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state and does not change the account.

Sets a temporary password for a person (C-4, 04 D-21, 04 D-24). Only the basic rule applies (length 8 to 64, no control
characters, a number, a symbol); a broken rule is a 400 on `temporaryPassword`. Every session of the person ends at once, a
failed-password lockout ends, a notice that a Manager reset the password is emailed, and the next sign-in goes through the emailed
code and then asks for a new password. The answer is empty: the password is never returned, logged or stored in plain text. A
Manager cannot do this to their own account (422 `users.own-account`) and a deactivated or locked person is a 422
`users.blocked`. It takes no version: it acts on the latest state.

Lifts a person's Manager lock (USER-03, D-16). The 15-minute failed-password lockout, if one is running, is left alone. Repeating
it on a person who is not locked is a 204 that changes nothing. It takes no version.
